title: Check your understanding: Tree Objects in Detail

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of tree objects in detail?
options: A tree object records names, modes and object IDs for entries in a directory snapshot. It represents directory structure rather than a mutable folder or a list of filesystem timestamps.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: A tree object records names, modes and object IDs for entries in a directory snapshot. It represents directory structure rather than a mutable folder or a list of filesystem timestamps.
questions.explanation: A tree object records names, modes and object IDs for entries in a directory snapshot. It represents directory structure rather than a mutable folder or a list of filesystem timestamps.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git ls-tree HEAD` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with tree objects in detail?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
